title: One Binary, Sim and Bench: The Same Controller and Scenario Against Either, and the Gap Between Them Measured

questions.question: What is the surest way to keep a simulation and a robot from diverging?
options: Have no second controller: the controller is the same program, and the choice of what is on the other side is configuration made when it starts
Review both controllers whenever either is changed
Build both with the same compiler and flags
Run both every night and compare the logs
questions.explanation: Two copies of a controller drift apart however carefully they are reviewed. One program, told at start up what it is talking to, has nothing to drift from.

questions.question: A configuration has 8 lines, every one wrong. What should the parser do?
options: Stop at the first bad line and report it
Use the default for every bad line and start
Report all 8 with their line numbers and leave the settings as they were: a program that starts with half a configuration is one no one can describe
Start with the lines that could be read
questions.explanation: Every bad line is reported with its number, and nothing is applied. A program running on half of what was asked for is in a state nobody chose.

questions.question: The bench is set up with no delay and no loss, and the simulation is run on the same scenario. What should the difference be?
options: Small but not zero, since the bench has a link
About the noise floor, 0.0053
Nothing: 0.0000 rms, since set up to be the same they must be the same, and if they differ the difference is a bug in a backend
Half a percent, from rounding in the link
questions.explanation: With no delay, no loss and no noise the bench backend is the simulation's plant reached another way. Any difference then is a mistake in one of them.

questions.question: The bench has a link delay of 2 ticks each way. Which sensor delay in the simulation matched it best?
options: 2, the link's delay one way
4, the round trip of the link, which cut the difference from 0.1901 to 0.0772
0: the simulation has no link to delay
8, twice the round trip
questions.explanation: A command takes 2 ticks to arrive and the measurement 2 to come back. A sensor delay of 4 ticks stands in for that round trip.

questions.question: After matching the delay the gap was still 0.0772, far above the noise floor of 0.0053. What is left?
options: Noise, which no model can match
The plant model, which is wrong
The controller's gain
What the simulation still lacks: the 5 percent loss, which a delay cannot imitate
questions.explanation: Two bench runs differ by 0.0053, so noise accounts for little of 0.0772. What the simulation has no way to imitate with a delay is frames that never arrive.

questions.question: Why does the trace record the plant's true position and not the measured one?
options: The measured position is not stored
The true position is cheaper to record
So that the controller can use it
The judge and the comparison are about what the plant did, and the measurement is what the controller was told: a late or noisy sensor would otherwise hide in the answer
questions.explanation: The controller only ever sees the measurement. The tools that judge the run need what really happened, or a bad sensor would make a bad run look good.
